newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam tells writers to work for revolution.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam tells writers to work for revolution.

text.p: Vietnam, facing threats to its ruling Communist Party, indicated on Monday it was seeking greater involvement of writers and artists in moves to promote socialism.

Communist Party chief Do Muoi told members of the Vietnam Writers Association -- a state-run forum -- that literary works should reflect popular aspirations for "the genial, the good, and the beautiful".
"The writers should wholeheartedly attach themselves to the country's great revolution, doing their best to write for the people and the country," the party daily, Nhan Dan, quoted him as saying.

Muoi added that "artistic labourers" should focus on building a virtuous society with a healthy ideology, lifestyle, soul and feelings by helping to spread understanding of this year's Communist Party congress.
Vietnam's artistic and literary traditions are relatively unknown outside the country, partly because of years or war and isolation.

Like other communist states, writers are encouraged to contribute to the socialist cause, but literary freedoms are seen as having increased in recent years allowing writers to tackle, albeit indirectly, issues once considered taboo.
The Communist Party has stepped up its efforts over the past year to promote orthodox socialist ideology and the leading role of the party.
Analysts say the move reflects concern about the adverse impact on Vietnam's majority young population of foreign cultural and other influences.
